newsitem.title: USA: Dow extends rebound as tobacco shares spark rally.
newsitem.headline: Dow extends rebound as tobacco shares spark rally.

text.p: U.S. blue chips soared for a third straight session on Wednesday, ignited by a sharp rally in tobacco stocks.

The Dow surged 93 points, or 1.4 percent, to close unofficially at 6680. With the gains, the average has now reversed 288 points, or more than 40 percent, of the nearly 700 points it lost between March 11 and April 11.
Philip Morris Cos Inc led the advance, jumping 4-1/8 to 43-1/8 on news that tobacco executives were negotiating to settle the massive litigation against the industry.

The talks, aimed at settling Medicaid-related lawsuits, were confirmed by Minnesota Attorney General Hubert Humphrey. The news quickly sparked new life into tobacco shares and helped stocks advance despite a weak performance by bonds.
"We got off to a good start with the positive reaction to the potential tobacco settlement," said Charlie Crane, chief market strategist at Key Asset Management.
"This was the first time in a while that bonds were a touch soft and stocks were more than a touch strong," he said.
But even as blue chips were roaring ahead, many analysts focused on the broad market, which was fairly mixed.
Once again, technology shares were mostly shut out of the rally, resulting in a second consecutive decline for the Nasdaq Composite.
Also weaker were interest rate-sensitive groups such as banks, which met with early selling pressure after fresh data underscored the bustling pace of U.S. economic activity.
The data, which included strong industrial output and manufacturing capacity utilization figures, pushed the yield on the benchmark long bond up a basis point to 7.10 percent.
"This is not the kind of scenario from which bulls are born," said Dick Stein, vice president at U.S. Clearing Corp.
Among financial stocks, Chase Manhattan Corp fell 2-7/8 to 89-3/4 and Citicorp dipped 2-1/2 to 104-3/8.
Analysts said the interest rate environment meant the outlook for the group and the broad market remained cloudy despite the recent blue chip bounce.
"Stocks are still not inherently cheap, and after earnings are through, people will start focusing on Mr. Greenspan again and that's not going to bring joy," Stein said.
For now, however, earnings hold center stage, and several issues roared to solid advances during the session after stronger-than-expected profit reports.
Among companies whose results beat Wall Street estimates were Colgate-Palmolive Co, which rose 2-3/8 to 107-1/8, and Ford Motor Co, up 1-1/2 to 34-3/4.
In contrast, investors punished several companies where there was a hint of slower profit or revenue growth.
Clarify Inc dropped 9-3/4 to seven after the help-desk software developer said it expected little if any revenue growth in the second quarter.
The dim outlook drove down other stocks in Clarify's market niche. Remedy Corp tumbled 7-3/4 to 32-11/16 and Scopus Technology Inc slid 5-1/4 to 22-7/8.
National Education Corp rose 4-3/8 to 19-3/8 after publishing company Harcourt General Inc launched a $19.50-a-share cash tender offer for the company.
Harcourt said the offer represented a 15 percent premium over National Education's proposed stock merger with Sylvan Learning Systems Inc, announced last month.
Shares in Sylvan Learning rose one point to 30-1/8. Harcourt shares jumped 2-1/8 to 45.
The S&P 500 index rose 8.81 points to 763.53.
